arguments.content:
"""Line-oriented helpers."""

from __future__ import annotations


def line_range(text: str, first: int, last: int) -> list[str]:
    """Return lines ``first`` through ``last`` of ``text``, inclusive.

    Lines are numbered from 1, as in an editor. A ``last`` beyond the end of
    the text is clamped to the final line. Line endings are not included.

    Args:
        text: Input text.
        first: Number of the first line to return (1-based).
        last: Number of the last line to return (1-based, inclusive).

    Returns:
        The selected lines.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``first`` is less than 1 or ``last`` is less than
            ``first``.
    """
    if first < 1:
        raise ValueError("first must be at least 1")
    if last < first:
        raise ValueError("last must not be less than first")
    lines = text.splitlines()
    return lines[first - 1:last]

arguments.summary: Fixed `textkit.lines.line_range` in `src/textkit/lines.py` by changing `return lines[first:last]` to `return lines[first - 1:last]`. The slice was treating the 1-based, inclusive `first`/`last` arguments as 0-based slice indices (off by one), so `line_range("alpha\nbeta\ngamma", 1, 2)` returned only `['beta']`. Converting to a 1-based inclusive slice (`first - 1` to `last`) makes both endpoints inclusive, preserves Python's built-in clamping when `last` exceeds the final line, and keeps line endings stripped via `splitlines()`. Existing behavior is unchanged: `first < 1` and `last < first` still raise `ValueError`, and empty text still yields `[]`. All 65 tests in `tests/` pass, and I verified the acceptance criteria (inclusive 1-based indexing, clamping, stripped line endings, and required exceptions) directly.
